items.title: Insurers Have Already Told Wall Street Which Advantage Plans Die on December 31. Members Are the Last to Know, and the Letter Isn’t Due Until October 2.
items.summary: Insurers spent the summer telling Wall Street exactly which Medicare Advantage plans are disappearing on December 31. Enrolled members get a letter in October, a closing enrollment window in December, and a rare legal protection most will never realize they have.

items.title: UnitedHealth Stock Rises 39% in 6 Months: Should Investors Still Buy?
items.summary: UNH's 39% six-month rally reflects improving medical costs, stronger earnings estimates and a sharper focus on profitable businesses.

items.title: 1 High-Flying Stock for Long-Term Investors and 2 Facing Headwinds
items.summary: “You get what you pay for” often applies to expensive stocks with best-in-class business models and execution. While their quality can sometimes justify the premium, they typically experience elevated volatility during market downturns when expectations change.

items.title: DaVita (DVA) Has Investors Asking A Fresh Question
items.summary: DaVita (DVA) is back in focus after two meaningful developments. The company expanded its value based care partnership with Humana for chronic kidney disease patients and agreed to a US$15 million settlement related to a prior data breach. Investors have been reacting to this mix of partnership news and legal resolution with a share price that is still up 58.64% year to date, despite a 30 day share price return of down 20.32%. The 3 year total shareholder return of 90.54% points to momentum...

items.title: If Your Advantage Plan Ends December 31 and You Do Nothing, You Wake Up January 1 in Original Medicare With No Drug Coverage and No Medigap.
items.summary: Humana's non-renewal letters are already in the mail, and the deadline to act is closer than most affected members realize. Missing it by even one day changes what coverage options remain available and how much they cost.

items.title: UnitedHealth Stock Recovered Before Its Margins Did
items.summary: UnitedHealth (UNH) stock has gained about 41% since early March, and at roughly $400 a share the market has already paid for a recovery. The easy reading is that the turnaround is finished. It is not. One half got better over those six months, the other got worse, and the price reflects the good half.

items.title: Is UnitedHealth Finally Turning the Corner After a Tough 2025?
items.summary: UNH is showing signs of recovery as medical costs improve, Optum gains momentum and 2026 earnings guidance rises.

items.title: CVS Stock Has Left Its Peers Behind. Or Has It?
items.summary: The market has crowned this healthcare giant the winner of its group, but a look at the underlying business raises the question of whether the celebration started too soon.
